0.title: NextGenius Company and Learning Content
0.summary: This group covers NextGenius itself: who it is, where it is based, and how it helps Australian businesses. It also holds the blog guides on learning AI and networking in Sydney.
findings: NextGenius combines AI consulting with digital product development, and Next Genius Pty Ltd is the legal entity behind it.
It is located at 15 Broadway, Ultimo and runs the Australia OPC initiative.
Blog guides on Sydney AI meetups, networking events and learning paths link back to NextGenius and its Learn AI Sydney service.

1.title: AI Agent and Automation Workshops
1.summary: This group describes the hands-on workshops NextGenius runs on AI agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP), machine learning and automation. They are aimed at teams who want practical experience.
findings: Workshops cover AI agent design, MCP integrations, machine learning for business and harness engineering.
Harness engineering keeps AI agents reliable in production, using evaluation harnesses, observability, feedback loops and rollback.
Workshops are designed for teams wanting practical experience with agents, automation and connected systems.

2.title: One Person Company Planner and Network
2.summary: This group covers the free service planner, the enquiry forms and the proposed Australian One Person Company (OPC) network. It also says plainly which features are not available.
findings: The free planner turns five answers into an editable service plan, with a pricing model to validate.
The discovery call and expression of interest forms only prepare an email; nothing is sent or saved by the website.
Member marketplace, service-page publishing and paid programmes are stated as not available.

3.title: MathTutor Pro Learning App
3.summary: This group covers MathTutor Pro, a STEM learning app with tutors, progress tracking and a free learning checkup for families. It lists the tutors and the student groups the app serves.
findings: The free learning checkup gives families an AI-generated summary by email and covers selective, opportunity class and HSC readiness.
Named tutors are Mr. Wang for maths, Ms. Li for English and Mr. Zhang for science.
The app offers personalised learning paths, multi-device learning and progress tracking for families.

4.title: Sydney AI Meetups and Attendees
4.summary: This group covers the Sydney AI meetup and events community run by NextGenius and who it is for. It lists the intended attendee groups and what attendees learn.
findings: The monthly meetup covers agent design, MCP integrations, automation workflows and implementation lessons.
Events are designed for founders, engineers, operators, students, builders and business leaders.
Events aim to create long-term connections and hands-on education, and guided bootcamps are another way to learn.

5.title: Example Service Packages and Pricing
5.summary: This group describes example first packages for small Australian service businesses, with their delivery steps and pricing. It also covers support after launch.
findings: Example packages are Review and Action Plan, Training and Coaching, Content and Research, and Setup and Implementation.
Pricing includes a fixed fee per review, a fee per session or short programme, and a fixed project fee with milestones.
Delivery support after launch aims to stop solutions becoming shelfware.

6.title: LunchUp and Example Applications
6.summary: This group covers the example applications on the site, mainly LunchUp, a networking app, and the Sydney startup and AI ecosystem map. The examples show product experiences, not measured client outcomes.
findings: LunchUp offers curated introductions, professional matching, meetup planning, startup news and curated opportunities.
The ecosystem map lists startups, investors and organisations such as Atlassian and Canva.
The site states that the examples are not independently measured client outcomes.

7.title: AI Creative Studio Learning Game
7.summary: This group covers AI Creative Studio, a game-like 3D studio that teaches creative systems thinking. A challenge, tutor and critic loop guides learners.
findings: Learners build 3D block worlds balancing housing, ecology, culture and infrastructure.
The critic gives strengths, improvements and rubric scores, and the tutor guides the next move.
It is described as a product demonstration, not a measured client case study.

8.title: Workflow Automation and Custom Software
8.summary: This group covers NextGenius services for small and medium businesses: connecting systems, automating workflows and building custom software. It focuses on removing manual handovers.
findings: Connected tools work moves information between CRM, finance and support tools.
Custom software includes internal tools, customer portals, web platforms, dashboards and admin systems.
Services can also enhance existing digital products and operational systems.

9.title: Admin Automation and Knowledge Assistant Pilots
9.summary: This group covers admin automation and the internal knowledge assistant, and how pilots of them are evaluated. It lists the measures used.
findings: Admin and follow-up automation reduces copying, status chasing and missed handovers.
The internal knowledge assistant searches policies, procedures and templates.
Pilots measure time to find an answer, source accuracy, staff adoption, manual steps, turnaround time and exception rates.

10.title: Event to Workshop Pathway
10.summary: This group covers the suggested path for newcomers: start with the events page, join a workshop, then bring a team. It also covers the FAQ that helps visitors decide if NextGenius fits.
findings: The Curiosity to Capability Pathway runs from an event to a workshop, then a private team session or partnership.
Visitors are advised to start with the events page before exploring workshops, FAQs and resources.
The FAQ answers questions about AI meetups and networking events in Sydney.

11.title: RAG Knowledge Assistant for Staff
11.summary: This group covers knowledge systems and AI search, mainly an assistant that lets staff search business documents. It also covers internal help desks and customer-facing knowledge.
findings: The RAG knowledge assistant searches policies and procedures and gives source references and clear review points.
Internal help desks support staff questions and onboarding.
Customer-facing knowledge experiences can be included where appropriate.

12.title: AI Consulting and Opportunity Reviews
12.summary: This group covers the AI consulting and planning service, which works out where AI fits in a business. It includes opportunity reviews and roadmap planning.
findings: AI opportunity reviews cover operations, sales and admin teams.
Roadmap planning covers business priorities, costs and next steps.
Consulting also advises on when to use existing platforms versus custom solutions.

13.title: What Makes a Good AI Meetup
13.summary: This group lists the elements of a useful AI meetup in Sydney. It says what attendees should expect to get from one.
findings: A good meetup includes technical demos, applied business case studies and practical Q and A.
It leaves room for networking after the session.

14.title: Building for Adoption and Support
14.summary: This group covers how delivered solutions are made usable by the team. It covers documentation, training and support.
findings: Building for adoption includes documentation, training and a practical support path.
The support stage helps the team adopt and improve the solution.

15.title: Business Assistant Setup Service
15.summary: This group covers OpenClaw Assistant Setup, a service that sets up a personal or business assistant. It includes workflows and secure rollout.
findings: Setup includes assistant workflows linked to documents, systems and daily processes.
It includes support for secure rollout, testing and team adoption, and configuration can be tailored for managers.

16.title: Agent Skills and Capability Design
16.summary: This group covers a session on defining what an AI agent can do. It covers scoping skills, memory and testing.
findings: The session covers skill mapping and capability matrices.
It also covers memory, context management and state, plus testing and iterative improvement of agent behaviour.

17.title: Discover Stage of Delivery
17.summary: This group covers Discover, the first stage of the project delivery process. It looks at the process, users and bottlenecks.
findings: The delivery process is a path from a business problem to a working solution.
Discover seeks to understand process bottlenecks.

18.title: Discovery Call and Workshop Booking
18.summary: This group covers the discovery call that visitors can request. It is also how teams book a workshop.
findings: Visitors are asked to describe one workflow, bottleneck or idea.
Booking a workshop starts with a discovery call, then NextGenius designs a workshop fitting the team's goals.

19.title: Community, Guides and Scoped Projects
19.summary: This group covers the NextGenius community and the practical guides it shares. It also links community learning to scoped AI projects.
findings: The community is for people turning AI and professional expertise into practical products, services and businesses.
Practical projects give the community learning context, and community conversations inform implementation.

20.title: Strategy and Scoping Engagement
20.summary: This group covers Strategy and Scoping, a short engagement that defines the right first move before building. It includes workshops and a roadmap.
findings: It includes discovery workshops and produces a recommended roadmap.

21.title: Pilot and Prove Value Engagement
21.summary: This group covers a focused build for one practical use case, so teams can test value before wider rollout. It includes user testing.
findings: The engagement delivers a pilot assistant or automation for one use case and includes user testing.

22.title: Applied AI Workshop for Teams
22.summary: This group covers a private workshop for teams. It covers AI opportunities, tooling choices, rollout planning and hands-on examples.
findings: The workshop is for business teams and technical leads, with hands-on examples for Australian organisations.

23.title: AI Assistants from Company Knowledge
23.summary: This group covers turning a company's own information into useful AI assistants.
findings: Company knowledge is the source from which AI assistants are built.

24.title: Start With One Workflow
24.summary: This group covers the recommended starting point of one useful workflow. It includes a three-step operations example.
findings: The example flow captures the request and context, finds information and drafts, then reviews decisions and exceptions.

25.title: Scope Stage and Success Measures
25.summary: This group covers Scope, the delivery stage where the workflow, success measures and boundaries are agreed.
findings: Scope agrees the success measures for the project.

26.title: Design, Build and Rollout Engagement
26.summary: This group covers a broader delivery model for businesses that know their direction and need help reaching production. It includes change support.
findings: Change support is provided during rollout.

27.title: Builders and Creatives Packages
27.summary: This group covers builders and creatives who can offer a focused implementation or content package.
findings: Builders and creatives offer a focused package of implementation or content.

28.title: Delivery Tools and Templates
28.summary: This group covers delivery tools such as templates, enquiry handling and useful automation that make delivery easier.
findings: Delivery tools include templates explored to make service delivery easier.
